new_packages.label: קַדִּישׁ וְהַכֶּתֶר
new_packages.rationale: The Torah's second major section (lines 13–16) is a compressed analysis of the Kaddish prayer's words: 'יתגדל = תגי + דל; ישראל הוא בחינת תגי כי שרית עם אלקים; יתקדש = ת"ק שדי; רבא = באר ומשביע לכל חי רצון.' These six concepts all share the essential nature of the elevated, divine dimensions of Kaddish as a cosmic map. תגי and כתר are explicitly equated (tagi = the crown-ornaments = keter). ישראל is equated with תגי/כתר. ת"ק שדי is the divine name Shaddai parsed as the fullness of the crown's numerical value. באר (well) and רצון are equated ('mashbia lechol chay ratzon'). Note that רצון already appears in Package #2 — however in Package #2 it appears as a bechina of מלכות/כבוד, while here it would appear in its Kaddish dimension as the satisfying-well. The question of whether these are the same or different appearances of רצון is a judgment call; they could be the same package if the Kaddish concepts are seen as elaborating the same malkhut-ratzon domain. However, the Kaddish cluster introduces a clearly new tier — the keter/crown dimension — that does not belong with malkhut. Recommendation: if at least תגי, כתר, ישראל are confirmed as bechina edges for Torah #177, create this as a new crown/Kaddish package distinct from Package #2.
prerequisite_bechina_edges: כתר ↔ ישראל (explicit: 'ישראל הוא בחינת תגי, כי שרית עם אלקים')
באר ↔ רצון (explicit: 'רבא – באר, ומשביע לכל חי רצון')
ת"ק שדי — isolated 1-node concept (from 'ויתקדש = ת"ק שדי'); needs a bechina partner to enter the graph
new_packages.threshold_met: Partially — the three-node cluster {תגי, כתר, ישראל} is fully supported by the text as a self-contained bechina-connected triad (3 concepts, 2 edges). This meets the 3+ concept threshold. The additional nodes (באר, רצון, ת"ק שדי) would expand it further. Recommend confirming and entering the missing bechina edges.

new_packages.label: מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה וְרָצוֹן אַחֵר
new_packages.rationale: The Torah explicitly describes the evil mirror of Package #2: 'כשרוצה האדם איזה רצון אחר חוץ מרצון השם יתברך, על ידי זה נעשה מלכות אחרים של העכו"ם.' This is the structural negative: just as holy ratzon → holy malkhut, so alien ratzon → malkhut acheim (foreign/evil kingdom). These two concepts share the essential nature of will-divorced-from-God as the generative source of evil dominion. Per the framework's principle of the good/evil mirror, this evil package is the direct counterpart of Package #2 (מלכות/כבוד/רצון). The text even specifies gradation: 'וכפי הרצון האחר, כן נעשה איזה מלכות לאיזה עכו"ם' — different degrees of alien will generate different foreign kingdoms. Only 2 nodes are identified in the source text for this domain. This does NOT meet the 3+ concept threshold for a new package independently, but it is strongly recommended as a 2-node evil-mirror package. A third node could be added if 'עכו"ם' (idolaters) is treated as a bechina of 'מלכות אחרים' — the text implies this ('מלכות אחרים של העכו"ם').
new_packages.threshold_met: Not yet — only 2 nodes confirmed. With the addition of עכו"ם as a third node (bechina of מלכות אחרים), the threshold would be reached.

observations: Torah #177 reveals a three-tier structure: (1) the humble-Jacob dimension (עקב/דל/יעקב = Package 1), (2) the will-kingdom dimension (מלכות/כבוד/רצון = Package 2), and (3) the consciousness-crown dimension (ראש/מחין = Package 3). The source text adds a fourth, as-yet unrecorded tier: the Kaddish-crown cluster (תגי/כתר/ישראל = proposed NP-1). The evil mirror exists for Package 2 (proposed NP-2: מלכות אחרים/רצון אחר). The overall argument of the Torah maps onto these tiers: wine→mochin (Tier 3, NP-1's crown aspect) → atonement → Kaddish → the proper enthronement of malkhut (Package 2) by total submission of will, in contrast to alien will that creates evil malkhut (NP-2). The Kaddish analysis connects all tiers: יתגדל = Package 1 (דל=יעקב); יתקדש = NP-1 (שדי); ויַמְלִיךְ מַלְכוּתֵהּ = Package 2 (malkhut rooted in ratzon); רבא = NP-1's well-of-ratzon. The Torah is structured as a Kabbalistic commentary on Kaddish, with the bechina-map tracing the spiritual anatomy encoded in each word.
